sections.h2: Selling a house in Hampden Township
sections.html:
Hampden Township ranks among the pricier, owner-dominated parts of the Harrisburg area and is Cumberland County's most populous municipality. An estimated 35,401 people lived here in 2025, an 8.1 percent rise since April 2020. Survey years 2020 to 2024 show owners in 76.9 percent of homes, a typical owned home valued at $354,900 and rent at $1,466. The median household income is $105,434.

Sellers in Hampden often own a family home with plenty of equity, and buyers want it in good shape. A house that needs repairs, holds tenants or arrived through an estate can sit on the market, so some owners price an as-is sale before paying for fix-ups. The Cumberland Valley School District serves the township and mails its own bill, described below.

sections.h2: Property tax bills and due dates
sections.html:
Each year an owner gets three bills: one from the county that also carries the library and township charges, one from the school district, and a per capita tax on adults. Assessed values are set by the county at 100 percent of 2010 value.

Real estate bill calendar
BillIssued2 percent discountFace amount10 percent penalty starts
County, library and townshipMarch 1March 1 to April 30May 1 to June 30July 1
Cumberland Valley School DistrictJuly 1July 1 to August 31September 1 to October 31November 1

The combined county, library and township millage is 3.031 mills for 2025 (county 2.625, library 0.250, township 0.156), and the school district rate is 11.937 mills for 2024 to 2025. Apply those mills to the assessed value, not to the sale price.

  • A county bill pays for a calendar year, and a school bill pays for July through June, so the closing agent splits each at the settlement date.
  • The per capita tax is $10 at face for each resident 18 or older. It is not prorated, so someone who moves out of the township after March 1 still owes the full year.
  • Landlords must tell the tax collector about tenants over 18 under Chapter 24 of the township code.
  • The state Homestead credit on the school bill was $85.49 for 2024 for residents on file with the county assessor.

Get a balance statement for your parcel from the tax collector before you sign a sale contract. For assessed value questions, the Cumberland County Assessment Office is at (717) 240-6350.

The township bills trash and stormwater, and both charges stay with the property, so clear them before closing. Weekly household pickup is $117.99 per quarter and includes one bulk item a week if you schedule it with the hauler.

The Sewer Authority set the stormwater fee by a 2015 resolution at $13.25 per equivalent residential unit each quarter. Every single-family home counts as one unit of 3,534 square feet of impervious surface. When the closing date is set, ask the township office about the sewer bill and a final reading.

Leaf collection, yard waste and bulk pickup schedules are on the township website. A clean, cleared yard helps a buyer walking the property, whether the buyer is a family or an investor.

Community Development, the township department that issues permits, expects one for most work above $500. Buyers and lenders sometimes ask whether past projects were closed out. The office works weekdays until 4:30 in the afternoon, and the phone is (717) 761-0119.

  • Building permits cover residential construction above $500 in total cost. Roof re-shingling that is not structural, window replacement, siding, gutters and like-for-like kitchen or bath replacement are exceptions.
  • Most standard residential permits are processed within 15 business days.
  • Zoning permits are needed for sheds, fences, accessory buildings and added impervious coverage.
  • A certificate of occupancy proves a building passed final inspection under the Pennsylvania Uniform Construction Code. The owner, not the contractor, is responsible for making sure it was issued.

A deck, pool or addition without its final inspection can hold up a sale that depends on a lender. Cash buyers may take that risk, though it is smart to ask the department how to close the file.

sections.h2: Recording and transfer tax in Cumberland County
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded by the Cumberland County Recorder of Deeds, with records back to 1750. Visits happen on weekdays until 4 in the afternoon, by appointment only. Book one at 717-240-6370.

Pennsylvania's realty transfer tax is 1 percent, and a local share is added at the recorder's office for school districts and municipalities. Property received by heirs, with a will or without, is exempt. The Department of Revenue's Cumberland County valuation factor is 1.56 for deeds accepted in the year that began July 1, 2026. Your title company can give you the exact local percentage and who pays each part.

After you accept an offer, the title company opens its search and asks for tax balances. Expect it to contact the tax collector and the township for trash and stormwater accounts, so give it the information promptly. If a mortgage is open, request a payoff from your lender.

Closing day is when you sign the deed and the settlement papers. The recorder then adds the deed to the county records. A cash buyer needs no appraisal or loan approval, so the schedule depends mostly on title work and any permit that has to be closed. Tell the buyer about the county and school bill periods early, since the settlement sheet will split each one between you at the closing date.

The right route depends on how the house looks and how fast you need to close.

  • Agent listing: usually the best price for a well-kept house, with showings, an appraisal and a lender's timetable to manage.
  • By owner: no listing fee, though you do the marketing, the forms and the negotiating.
  • Cash offer: the buyer accepts the house as it stands, with no showings and no repair list, and closes on a date you pick.

If repairs were put off, an estate is open or tenants live there, measure each route by what you keep and not by the sticker price.

Request a balance statement for each bill from the tax collector, then check the trash and stormwater accounts. Look for permits that were never finished and ask Community Development how to close them. The title company can tell you the local transfer tax share and who pays what.

With a tenant in the house, hand the buyer the lease and recall the landlord reporting rule for tenants over 18. If a relative left you the house, gather the papers that prove you can sign for the estate. Last, line up written offers and compare them on proceeds and on closing speed.

faqs.q: Can a Hampden house be sold while a tax bill is unpaid?
faqs.a: Yes. A sale can close with an open balance. Call the township tax collector at (717) 737-4822 for your parcel's figure and give it to the title company, so it shows on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Who handles a wrong Hampden assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Cumberland County Assessment Office at (717) 240-6350. The township tax collector only bills the assessed value the county provides, so corrections and appeals start with the county.

faqs.q: Does the per capita tax follow me if I sell and move mid-year?
faqs.a: Yes, if you lived in the township on March 1, when bills were mailed. There is no proration, so Hampden Township gets the full amount for that year and not your new municipality.

faqs.q: Is a certificate of occupancy needed to sell in Hampden?
faqs.a: It is proof that permitted work passed final inspection. If a past project needed a permit, phone Community Development at (717) 761-0119 and confirm the last inspection took place before you list.

faqs.q: What does the Hampden stormwater fee cost?
faqs.a: The Sewer Authority set it in 2015 at $13.25 per quarter for each equivalent residential unit, and a single-family home counts as one. Check today's amount with the township before closing.
